title: Adaptive degradation and multi-region fallback for downstream store resilience (Redis/Kafka/DB)
creator: Priya Sharma
description:
Problem: During bursts and partial region/network degradations, downstream dependencies (Redis, Kafka, and primary DB) are the dominant source of tail latency and request failures. Existing protections rely on coarse connection pooling and static circuit-breakers which either over-triage healthy regions or fail to protect latency SLOs when a region partially degrades.

Goal: Implement an adaptive degradation strategy that: 1) rapidly detects degrading dependency health at regional granularity; 2) applies graded admission control, request grading (best-effort vs guaranteed), and transparent local degradation (read-only cache, stale-serve TTL extension) to preserve frontend SLOs; 3) orchestrates multi-region fallback for reads and buffered async writes for Kafka/DB when appropriate; and 4) exposes observability and runbook actions in the Console.

This ticket covers design and a first-phase implementation for Redis/Kafka/DB on the serving runtime and control plane hooks for rollout and observability.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive circuit-breaker detects dependency error-rate/latency deviation within 10s and flips modes with <5% false-positive rate during synthetic fault injection
Per-region admission control enforces token-bucket or priority lanes such that p99 tail latency for gen/chat endpoints remains within SLO during injected downstream slowdowns
Reads can transparently degrade to local (prefix) cache or stale-serve with a documented TTL extension policy and correctness guardrails
Writes to Kafka/DB can be buffered and retried with bounded memory and backpressure signals; no unbounded in-memory queues after 30m of sustained outage
Console dashboard surfaces region-level dependency health, circuit-breaker state, admission rates, and per-model degraded-serve fraction
Canary rollout plan documented and executed on a small fleet without customer-visible errors; rollback path validated
design_summary:
We will implement an adaptive failure controller composed of three cooperating layers: (A) Local runtime health detector using sliding-window latency and error histograms per dependency and per-region; (B) Adaptive circuit-breaker that uses a hybrid of error-rate windows and latency percentiles with hysteresis and warmup; (C) Graded degradation controller that maps breaker state to admission policies and degradation modes.

Degradation modes (ordered, reversible): 
- Mode 0: Normal (full requests allowed).
- Mode 1: Priority lanes + backpressure (low-priority requests are shed by token-bucket).
- Mode 2: Read-degraded: reads served from local cache/prefix KV or stale-serve with TTL bump; writes still allowed but rate-limited.
- Mode 3: Write-buffered: synchronous writes buffered to durable local spool + async flush to Kafka/DB; system exposes graceful error for non-critical writes.
- Mode 4: Regional failover: traffic routed to a healthy region for read-heavy flows; write flows are either buffered or proxied per policy.

Circuit-breaker will support configurable thresholds per dependency type, per-region and per-tenant overrides. Admission uses token-bucket with dynamic refill tuned by observed throughput and target latency headroom. A global soft-budget ensures memory bound for write buffers and prevents cascading failures.
implementation_notes: Runtime: Add per-dependency detector instrument in the RPC path that records rolling windows of success/latency/error; provide light-weight shared-memory structure for fast reads
Circuit-breaker: Implement hybrid sliding-window (exponentially decayed counts) + p99-latency trigger; add cooldown/hysteresis and 'probe' sampling during cooldown to reassess health
Admission control: Add request priority header and token-bucket admission in front of dependency calls. Low-priority requests receive 429 or a degraded content path depending on mode
Read-degrade: Leverage existing prefix/KV cache logic to serve reads; add TTL extension mechanism with safety checks (max-staleness per route) and a 'validation probe' to avoid long-term divergence
Write-buffer: Durable spool on local node (append-only file rotated and bounded) with backpressure exposed up the stack; a separate background flusher with exponential backoff per target region
Multi-region routing: Extend smart-routing policy to allow region-targeted fallbacks for reads; for writes default to buffering unless user has opted-in for cross-region writes
Control plane: Expose breaker state and metrics via telemetry and provide an API for emergency override and testing
Config: Provide sane defaults; enable feature via feature-flag per cluster and allow per-customer tuning via Console
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Merge feature-gated code behind runtime flag; unit and integration tests in CI
Stage 1: Internal canary on non-customer dev cluster for 48h with synthetic fault injection (latency and error increase)
Stage 2: Canary to 2% of customer traffic in a single region for 72h; monitor SLOs & alerts
Stage 3: Incremental ramp to 25% across two regions; enable multi-region fallback for read-only flows only
Stage 4: Full fleet rollout with documentation to SRE and on-call; runbook published and automated rollback if key alerts fire
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics: per-dependency per-region error_rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies, breaker_state (enum), admission_rejections, buffered_writes_count, spool_disk_usage
Alerts: pager if breaker enters Mode 3+ for >5 minutes in production or if buffered_writes_count grows > 10k or spool_disk_usage > 80%
Dashboards: Console panel showing regional comparison, percentage of requests in each degradation mode, and impact on user-visible latency
SLOs: Maintain 99th percentile tail latency within configured headroom for critical routes; Surface a degraded-serve metric to quantify functional impact
test_plan: Unit tests for detector, circuit-breaker transitions, and admission controller edge cases
Integration tests that simulate partial region packet loss, injected latency on Redis/Kafka/DB, and verify mode transitions
Chaos tests in staging: throttle Redis for single region, validate failover routing and buffer behavior
Performance: benchmark p95/p99 under normal and degrade modes to ensure added overhead <5% on happy-path
Game-day runbook drill with SRE to exercise emergency override and rollback
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives flipping breakers and causing unnecessary fallback. Mitigation: conservative defaults, probe sampling during cooldown, and telemetry to detect oscillation
Risk: Buffered writes leading to data loss on node loss. Mitigation: durable spool, bounded retention, and replication of spool metadata to control plane if enabled
Risk: Increased complexity of routing causing operational burden. Mitigation: phased rollout, good observability, and clear runbooks; defaults for most customers
Risk: Cross-region consistency violations when serving stale reads. Mitigation: per-route max-staleness config and validation probes for critical routes
